title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for type 2 diabetes and polyneuropathy.

HPI
The patient is an 85-year-old male presenting for a routine follow-up of his type 2 diabetes mellitus. He reports that his peripheral neuropathy symptoms remain stable, characterized by mild tingling in his toes. He continues to manage his glucose levels using a combination of long-term insulin therapy and an oral hypoglycemic agent. He denies any recent acute changes in his symptoms or any significant side effects from his current regimen.

Medication List
- Insulin
- Metformin
- Lisinopril

Exam
The patient appears well-nourished and in no acute distress. Neurological exam reveals diminished sensation to light touch in the bilateral feet. Skin is intact without ulcers or signs of infection.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Stable on current dual therapy.
2. Polyneuropathy: Symptoms are currently managed.

Plan
Continue the current regimen of insulin and metformin. We will monitor his laboratory values at the next visit to ensure continued stability. The patient will return in three months for a follow-up evaluation.

Electronically signed, P. O'Brien, MD, 05/14/2026
explanations: Polyneuropathy is listed under 'with' for diabetes: the combination code E11.42 captures both.
When both insulin and oral hypoglycemics are used, assign both Z79.4 and Z79.84.

distractors.why: Coding the two separately misses the presumed link.
Both Z codes are assigned when both drug types are used.
